usage: xo run [--seed=N] [--record=trace.xotrace] [--holes] [--backend=go|llvm|arm64|amd64]
              [--no-gc] [--no-mono] [--no-arenas] [--tzdata=embedded|system]
              [--profile=cpu|heap|cpu,heap] [--trace=FILE] [--race]
              [--stamp NAME=VALUE]... [--watch [--grace=D]] [dir] [-- args...]

Build for the host and run the program in dir (default .) with args.
xo run runs exactly that directory and never one below it (decision
0345): a dir with no .xo file or no main is an error.
--seed makes task interleavings reproducible: one thread runs the
tasks and a generator seeded with N picks the next at each scheduling
point (decision 0350). --record writes every
effect (clock, rand, env, stdin, fs, net, http client responses, server
requests, signals) and every scheduling decision into the trace (core
11.3) for xo replay. --holes allows holes (???), which fault when
evaluated. --record needs the Go backend. --profile=cpu
samples the program's CPU time (a native backend, the host's by default)
into xo-cpu.pprof (go tool pprof reads it) and a text summary,
xo-cpu.txt, in the working directory; --profile=heap samples its
allocations into xo-heap.pprof and xo-heap.txt; cpu,heap takes both. A
profile file that exists is not overwritten. --trace=FILE records the
scheduler's execution trace (XO_TRACE, a native backend; decision 0240)
into FILE, then writes FILE.json for ui.perfetto.dev and prints a summary
(xo trace). --watch rebuilds after a change to the module's sources and
restarts the program only when the built binary changed (an edit to a
test or a comment does not restart it): SIGTERM, up to --grace (5s) for
it to exit, then SIGKILL; a failed build keeps the old program running.
With --json each cycle is a JSON line, the last also in
last.json in the watch's cache directory, <user cache>/xo/watch/HASH
(decision 0267); the watch writes nothing into the project.
